metadata.description: Emergency red flag symptoms for triage classification
metadata.disclaimer: This is for AI triage assistance only. Always err on the side of caution.

context_indicators: radiating to arm, jaw, neck, or back
questions: Is the pain crushing, pressure-like, or squeezing?
Does the pain radiate to your arm, jaw, neck, or back?
Are you sweating profusely?
Do you feel short of breath?
Do you feel nauseous or lightheaded?
Does the pain occur at rest or with exertion?
How long have you had this pain?
critical.immediate_action: Call emergency services immediately. Do not drive yourself.

questions: What is your current blood pressure reading?
Do you have a severe headache?
Are you experiencing vision changes?
Do you have chest pain?
critical.immediate_action: Seek immediate medical attention.

context_indicators: lasting more than a few minutes
questions: How long have you been experiencing palpitations?
Are you also feeling dizzy or lightheaded?
Do you have any chest discomfort?
Do you have a history of heart problems?
Is your heartbeat regular or irregular?
Can you smile? Does one side of your face droop?
Can you raise both arms? Does one arm drift downward?
Can you repeat a simple sentence? Is your speech slurred?
When did these symptoms start?
Do you have a sudden severe headache?
critical.immediate_action: Call emergency services immediately. Note the time symptoms started.
critical.mnemonic: FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call 911

questions: Is this the worst headache you've ever had?
Did it come on suddenly, like a thunderclap?
Do you have a stiff neck?
Do you have a fever?
Have you had any recent head injury?
Are you confused or having trouble thinking?
critical.immediate_action: Call emergency services immediately.

questions: Is this the first time you've had a seizure?
How long did the seizure last?
Did you lose consciousness?
Did you bite your tongue or lose bladder control?
Have you had any recent head injury?
critical.immediate_action: Call emergency services for first-time seizure or if seizure lasts >5 minutes.

questions: Did the vision loss occur suddenly?
Is one eye or both eyes affected?
Is there any pain?
Do you see flashing lights or new floaters?
Do you have diabetes or high blood pressure?

context_indicators: unable to speak in full sentences
history of asthma/COPD not responding to rescue inhaler
questions: Can you speak in full sentences?
Are your lips or face turning blue?
Do you feel like you're suffocating?
Is there associated chest pain?
Did this come on suddenly?
If you have asthma/COPD, did your rescue inhaler help?
critical.immediate_action: Call emergency services immediately. Sit upright if possible.

context_indicators: swelling of lips, tongue, or throat
questions: Are your lips, tongue, or throat swelling?
Are you having difficulty breathing or swallowing?
Do you have widespread hives or rash?
Were you recently exposed to something you're allergic to?
Do you have an EpiPen?
critical.immediate_action: Use EpiPen if available. Call emergency services immediately.

questions: Can you speak or make sounds?
Are you able to cough?
Did this happen while eating?
critical.immediate_action: If cannot breathe/cough/speak: Begin Heimlich maneuver. Call emergency services.

questions: How much blood are you coughing up?
Is it bright red or dark?
Do you have chest pain?
Are you short of breath?
Do you have a history of lung disease or blood clots?

context_indicators: has means to carry out plan
questions: Are you having thoughts of hurting yourself?
Do you have a plan for how you would do it?
Do you have access to the means to carry out your plan?
Have you made any preparations (giving away items, writing notes)?
Have you attempted suicide before?
Are you currently under the influence of drugs or alcohol?
critical.immediate_action: Do not leave the person alone. Call emergency services or suicide hotline (988 in US).

questions: Are you currently injured?
Is there active bleeding?
Do you need immediate medical attention for your injuries?
Are you safe right now?
critical.immediate_action: Seek immediate medical attention for injuries. Contact mental health crisis services.

questions: Are you seeing or hearing things others don't?
Do you feel like someone is trying to harm you?
Are you having thoughts of hurting yourself or others?
Are you currently taking any medications or substances?
critical.immediate_action: Ensure safety. Contact emergency services if danger to self or others.

questions: Is this the first time you've experienced this?
Does this feel different from your usual panic attacks?
Do you have chest pain or pressure?
Are you sweating profusely?
Do you have a history of heart problems?
high.note: Must rule out cardiac emergency before attributing to anxiety

questions: How severe is the pain on a scale of 1-10?
Where exactly is the pain located?
Did it start suddenly or gradually?
Is your abdomen tender or rigid to touch?
Are you vomiting blood or passing blood in stool?
For women: Is there any chance you're pregnant?
critical.immediate_action: Seek immediate medical attention. Do not eat or drink.

questions: Are you vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds?
Are your stools black and tarry?
Is there bright red blood in your stool?
Do you feel dizzy or faint?
Are you taking blood thinners or NSAIDs?
Do you have liver disease or history of ulcers?
critical.immediate_action: Call emergency services immediately.

questions: How long have you been unable to keep fluids down?
When did you last urinate?
Are you feeling confused or disoriented?
Is your heart racing?
Are you experiencing dizziness when standing?

context_indicators: clear fluid from ear or nose
questions: Did you lose consciousness? For how long?
Are you confused or having trouble remembering what happened?
Have you vomited?
Is there clear fluid draining from your ear or nose?
Do you have a severe headache?
Are your pupils different sizes?
critical.immediate_action: Call emergency services. Do not move if spinal injury suspected.

questions: Is the blood spurting or flowing heavily?
Have you applied direct pressure for 10-15 minutes?
How much blood have you lost (estimate)?
Are you feeling dizzy, cold, or confused?
critical.immediate_action: Apply firm direct pressure. Call emergency services. Use tourniquet if limb and life-threatening.

context_indicators: neck or back pain after trauma
questions: Can you move your arms and legs?
Do you have feeling in your arms and legs?
Did this happen after a fall, dive, or car accident?
Do you have neck or back pain?
critical.immediate_action: DO NOT MOVE. Call emergency services immediately. Keep still until help arrives.

questions: How old is the baby?
What is the rectal temperature?
Is the baby feeding normally?
Is the baby lethargic or unusually irritable?
Has the baby had any vaccines recently?
critical.immediate_action: Seek immediate medical attention. Fever in infants under 3 months is a medical emergency.

questions: When was the last wet diaper?
Does the child have tears when crying?
Is the soft spot on the head sunken?
Is the child alert or lethargic?
Has there been vomiting or diarrhea?
critical.immediate_action: Seek immediate medical attention.

questions: Do you have diabetes?
When did you last eat?
When did you last take your diabetes medication/insulin?
Are you feeling confused or disoriented?
Are you sweating and shaking?
Can you check your blood sugar?
critical.immediate_action: If conscious and able to swallow, give sugar. If unconscious, call emergency services. Do not give anything by mouth if unconscious.

questions: How many weeks pregnant are you?
Are you experiencing vaginal bleeding?
Is there severe abdominal pain?
Have you noticed decreased fetal movement?
Do you have a severe headache or vision changes?
Is there sudden swelling of hands or face?
Are you leaking fluid?
critical.immediate_action: Call emergency services or go to labor and delivery immediately.

HIGH.response_time: Go to ER or urgent care within 2-4 hours

LOW.description: Routine, can wait for regular appointment

general_questions.duration: How long has this been going on?
general_questions.severity: On a scale of 1-10, how severe is this?
general_questions.progression: Is it getting better, worse, or staying the same?
general_questions.associated_symptoms: Are you experiencing any other symptoms?
general_questions.interventions: Have you tried anything to help? Did it work?
general_questions.medical_history: Do you have any relevant medical history?
